answer_quotes: Er, cos I don’t feel that I can do business. When I see my father running a business, I find it quite hard er there’s not really a regular schedule.
And I found that more – erm satisfying things in engineering because I’d like to say I did this bridge, or something.

Mm, no. Actually it was a friend of mine. I was thinking to do science subjects and he said he’s studying about engineering and that idea came across my mind and I started to think it could be a good idea.

My family, they are neutral – my mother actually said it could be quite tough for a girl to do civil engineering, but, I think, or yeah, I’d like – yeah, I think I’d like the course so…and engineering discipline can go to business sector as well.
I like the infrastructure, I think. I was thinking to do materials as well but I decided to do civil, that’s all.
I’d love to do politics and literature, but since I don’t apply to Hong Kong, after I’ve graduated I don’t think it’s easy for me to have a career on that path.
Yeah, I really like it.

It’s just I think I’ve learned a lot more but at first I didn’t know what to expect from the course. So everything’s quite a surprise and new for me. But I like it. Some modules they are quite boring and er, coursework they are quite hard but most of all I find it quite interesting and the lecturers they are willing to – to teach and they are patient.
I think the male lecturers tend to go faster you know – at a faster pace. Erm, and I think my female lecturer got a special way to lecture, so it’s quite hard to compare.
Yes, I think I’ve become a different person, or a stronger person.
Erm, sometimes my group mate will not turn up on time or they just disappeared. It’s quite annoying sometimes.
Er, I think they are quite fair on the mental work. On the physical work they might help you.
Because I want some experiences in the civil industry and hopefully I can get the job easier after I graduate.
My Dad told me not to go on placement. Yeah, he thinks it’s better to finish university earlier but I believe it’s better to have some experience.
First of all I know what civil engineering is really like. Erm, some technical skills because being on site for a year will be – probably will learn more than staying on at university and yeah.

The best thing is to get (?). To know more people and to larger your network and know what to expect after you graduate, when you go into work. The bad side is it’s very hard to handle the situation at times, I think, especially on site because I really have no idea what will happen there.
Erm, I’m applying to big companies (yes) because I like to travel around but I want to have something with company so that it looks better on my CV.
No, I do think I want to be an engineer, but I don’t know if I want to be consultant or contractor. And I think my placement experience will help me make the decision.
Er, I hope that I can be Chartered, or I’ll carry on and an MSc programme after the undergraduate.
Definitely being chartered. Hopefully I can be senior engineer or be responsible for quite large project and I can travel around.
I would prefer to go into contracting. But then I am thinking, I don’t know if I can handle the situations on site and it’s – it would be a more relaxing environment, in consultancy.
Not at the moment but eventually I think I’ll go into consulting because I wouldn’t imagine myself, at age 40, climbing up and down

Erm, I wouldn’t imagine it is hard to have a job but I really think that the salary is not very competitive (OK) because engineers are – they put in a lot of hard work. Erm, the starting salary’s good but after being a senior engineer, it’s not going very far.

And being a civil engineer, you might travel quite a bit and it’s very hard work but you might have to concentrate in your career totally, well having a family you have responsibility for your family and then I guess every female does – you start to think which is more important.
